What are Pragmatic Trials?

Pragmatic trials are designed to test interventions in real-world conditions, focusing on:

- **Real-world effectiveness** rather than controlled efficacy
- **Broad patient populations** with minimal exclusion criteria
- **Routine clinical settings** rather than specialized research environments
- **Practical outcomes** that matter to patients and clinicians
- **Rapid implementation** of findings into clinical practice

## Key Differences at a Glance

| Metric               | Pragmatic Trials (e.g., RECOVERY)    | Traditional Explanatory Trials                                                                      |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cost per Trial       | Lower due to existing infrastructure | $48-225 million [@anjusoftware-clinical-trial-costs]            |
| Time to Results      | Weeks to months                      | 5-7 years average [@phase-3-participant-numbers] |
| Participants         | Large (e.g., 47,000+ in RECOVERY)    | Typically 500-3000 [@trial-costs-fda-study]                         |
| Implementation Speed | Hours to days                        | Months to years                                                                                     |
| Patient Population   | Diverse, real-world                  | Highly selected                                                                                     |
| Setting              | Routine clinical practice            | Specialized research centers                                                                        |
| Generalizability     | High                                 | Limited                                                                                             |

![Pragmatic trials: cheap, fast, big. Explanatory trials: expensive, slow, small. One asks 'Does this work in the real world?' The other asks 'Does this work in a laboratory with perfect conditions?'](/assets/images/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials-section-key-differences-comparison-bw-academic.jpg)

## Speed and Efficiency

### RECOVERY Trial Metrics

![RECOVERY went from idea to policy in months while enrolling 47,000 people across 200 hospitals. Speed and scale at the same time. Possible when you skip the theater.](/assets/images/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials-section-recovery-trial-metrics-bw-academic.jpg)

- 9 days: Concept to first patient enrollment [@recovery-trial-dexamethasone-results]
- 10 weeks: First life-saving treatment identified [@landray-recovery-trial-quote]
- 3 hours: Results to policy implementation [@landray-recovery-trial-quote]
- 47,000+ participants across 6 countries [@recovery-trial-summary-quote]
- 200+ hospital sites [@recovery-trial-summary-quote]
- 10 major results obtained [@recovery-trial-summary-quote]
- 4 effective COVID-19 treatments identified [@recovery-trial-summary-quote]

### Traditional Trial Metrics

![Clinical trials take 7.2 years and fail constantly. You built a system where dying people have to wait longer than it takes to get through primary school.](/assets/images/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials-section-traditional-trial-metrics-bw-academic.jpg)

- Average time from phase 1 to approval: 7.2 years [@bio-clinical-development-success-rates-2006]
- 80% of trials fail to meet enrollment timelines [@clinical-trial-enrollment-timelines]
- Up to 50.0% of research sites enroll one or no patients [@clinical-trial-enrollment-timelines]

## Clinical Impact

### RECOVERY Trial

![Dexamethasone saved a million lives. The drug was invented in 1957. You just forgot to test it properly for 63 years.](/assets/images/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials-section-recovery-trial-bw-academic.jpg)

- Dexamethasone findings [@recovery-trial-dexamethasone-results]:
  - 35% reduction in mortality for ventilated patients
  - Estimated 1 million lives saved globally [@recovery-trial-summary-quote]

- Implementation within hours of results
- Real-world effectiveness immediately apparent

### Traditional Trials

- 14% success rate from phase 1 to approval [@pmc6092479]
- Average 7 years from discovery to clinical practice
- Limited real-world applicability due to strict inclusion criteria

## Advantages of Pragmatic Trials

![Four reasons pragmatic trials work better. Or as normal people call them, reasons to do the obvious thing.](/assets/images/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials-section-advantages-of-pragmatic-trials-bw-academic.jpg)

1. **Better Generalizability**

   - Results apply to broader patient populations
   - Findings directly relevant to routine clinical practice
   - Higher external validity

2. **Resource Efficiency**

   - Uses existing healthcare infrastructure
   - Lower per-patient costs
   - Faster recruitment and completion

3. **Implementation Speed**

   - Rapid translation to clinical practice
   - Immediate real-world validation
   - Reduced lag between evidence and practice

4. **Statistical Power**

   - Larger sample sizes possible
   - More diverse patient populations
   - Better representation of real-world outcomes
